name: Czechia
snapshot: Billionaire Andrej Babiš returned as prime minister with the hard right, promising "not a crown" of Czech money for Ukraine, while President Petr Pavel acts as a check.
culture: Prague's medieval centre and Charles Bridge are among Europe's most visited sights. The Czechs are among the world's least religious people and its biggest beer drinkers per head, with Pilsner born in Plzeň. Kafka, Kundera and Havel, the dissident playwright who became president, are literary icons. Ice hockey is the top sport.
society: The Czech Republic has one of the EU's lowest unemployment rates and a strong car industry led by Škoda. The 1989 Velvet Revolution and the 1993 peaceful split from Slovakia are points of pride. Babiš, whose companies have faced EU conflict of interest rulings, leads a populist coalition with the SPD and the Motorists.
situation: When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Czechia, which remembers Soviet tanks crushing the Prague Spring in 1968, became one of Kyiv's most energetic allies. Its biggest contribution was the "ammunition initiative," proposed in 2023: Czech dealers combed the world for artillery shells outside the EU and Western partners paid for them. Ukraine received millions of rounds. Then in October 2025 voters returned Andrej Babiš, a billionaire populist who had campaigned on ending it.

Babiš, whose ANO party now governs with the hard-right SPD, took office in December promising "not a crown" of Czech money for Ukraine (dpa via GNA). In January 2026 he reversed course on the initiative itself: after allied pressure in Paris, he agreed Czechia would keep coordinating it, but only with others' money, and ruled out Czech troops in any Ukraine peace force (Kyiv Post). Funding for 760,000 shells in 2026 was already secured. He also published figures from the initiative that his predecessor Petr Fiala said were classified and endangered the companies and people involved (Ukrainska Pravda). Babiš still faces questions over his ownership of Agrofert, a farming and chemicals empire of more than 250 companies that he has promised to put in a trust, and his past fraud case over EU subsidies. President Petr Pavel, a former NATO general, acts as a check from Prague Castle.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the government with the confidence of the 200-seat Chamber of Deputies; the directly elected president appoints the prime minister and represents the country abroad.
holders: Prime Minister Andrej Babiš (ANO), since December 2025; President Petr Pavel.
